solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters sit inside the wise man's name

parts.note: Solon was the wise lawgiver of Athens, so a byword for a sage

indicators.note: cooking says the letters of mice are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook is told to stop putting mice in the sage stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' turns MICE into EMIC, which goes 'in' SOLON. 'Stop' is a punctuation mark here, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is a kind of stop, a pause in a written sentence.

clue.text: Clog from second monk's not black

indicators.note: not says the black letter is missing from the monk

parts.note: an abbot is a head monk; the 's is read as is
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A clog comes from a second monk who is not dressed in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monk's not black' reads as a monk without black robes, but it means the head monk minus the letter for black.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden shoe is a sabot, a peasant clog.

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
to linger is to dally or dawdle

explanation.surface: Mother dawdles and shirks her duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign illness to escape work or duty.

definitions.meaning: the folk song 'Oh my darling' names a miner's daughter with this name

explanation.surface: Fruit is offered to a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a citrus fruit and the girl addressed as 'my darling' in the old ballad.

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of Neil got turn ugly and jumbled

explanation.surface: Neil developed a nasty freckle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges NEIL GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names a small pigmented skin spot, a freckle or lentil-shaped mark.

clue.text: Wind could perhaps worsen with time

indicators.note: could perhaps suggests the letters of worsen might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wind could perhaps get worse as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could perhaps' turns WORSEN into NORWES; add T.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'wester is a wind from the north-west.

clue.text: Half a grape in the salad

indicators.note: half says only the front five of the ten letters of the grape variety are kept

parts.note: Chardonnay is a white wine grape

explanation.surface: Half a grape has found its way into the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' leaves CHARD from CHARDONNAY, losing ONNAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy vegetable whose young leaves are eaten raw among salad greens.

clue.text: Could be a double feature, getting a double toast

definitions.meaning: a double ... is a facial feature, so this part of the face could be doubled
the toast ...-... is this word said twice; half of it fills the light

explanation.surface: A double feature at the cinema is celebrated with a double toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means part of the face, not a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower face part can be double, and repeated it makes the toast chin-chin.

clue.text: Crime of clergyman losing his head

indicators.note: losing his head says the clergyman's first letter goes

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman's crime makes him lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' drops P from PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a crime.

definitions.meaning: the carrying out of a duty, as in the fulfilment of an obligation
to settle or pay off a debt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fulfilling a duty and settling what is owed, both doing and paying.

parts.note: the Bronte sisters wrote as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell, so a Bronte is a Bell
the initial E as written

explanation.surface: A lovely girl is named simply as Bronte E.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bronte sisters published under the surname Bell; Emily was Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired at a gathering.

parts.note: reads as the prime of young life, but names both a spring bloom and the beautiful youth of Greek myth who loved his reflection

explanation.walkthrough: In myth the vain youth was turned into the flower that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil genus and the mythical youth share the name, so it is a flower of a youth.

indicators.note: served suggests the letters are dished up in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fruit and an eastern gin are served up together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges EASTERN GIN, all ten letters, into the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: These small loose-skinned oranges are a citrus fruit.

indicators.note: headless says the first letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: a finch is a small seed-eating bird

explanation.surface: Someone measures a headless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes F from FINCH.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of length is a measure, one twelfth of a foot.

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: twelve of 12-across's measure make a foot
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A crossing is built from a dozen measures laid on a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve of the unit at 12-across make a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge for pedestrians is a crossing over a road, railway or river.

indicators.note: lost says those letters drop out of the whirlpool word

parts.note: L is the pound sign's letter and M is Roman for a thousand

explanation.surface: A famous conductor of a maelstrom has lost a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes L and M out of MAELSTROM in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is an honorific for an eminent orchestral conductor.

clue.text: School mistress and a boy with English conserve

parts.note: marm, as in schoolmarm, is a schoolmistress
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A schoolmistress and a boy with English share a conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus preserve is a conserve spread on toast.

clue.text: He swears about report about nothing

indicators.note: the second about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the zero
about here means scattered around, so the letters of report are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man swears about a report concerning nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' turns REPORT into TROPER; the second 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'swear like a trooper' makes a cavalry soldier the type of man who curses.

clue.text: Empty remark from priest on range

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: latitude is scope or range, freedom of action

explanation.surface: A priest's empty remark comes from the pulpit range.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite, hollow statement, an empty remark.

indicators.note: getting cut means the front letter is chopped off the word for gifts

parts.note: presents are gifts or donations

explanation.surface: Someone resents donations being reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cut' removes P from PRESENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it, to grudge it.

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters of the grass are spread about anew

explanation.surface: Esparto grass is distributed at Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPARTO is a grass used for paper; 'distributed' rearranges it. Dover is a Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is an example of a harbour town on the coast.

clue.text: Macbeth's query about his title? What a gas

definitions.meaning: Macbeth is hailed as Thane of Cawdor, so he might ask '...?'
a flammable natural gas, the main part of marsh gas

explanation.surface: Macbeth queries his title, and someone exclaims what a gas it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is Macbeth asking if he is a thane; it is also a hydrocarbon gas.

indicators.note: reviewing hints at looking over the letters again and recasting them

explanation.surface: An artist reviews the aims she has set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' rearranges SET AIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a famous artist.

parts.note: one is the article a
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: One orchestra plays as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition, too, besides.

clue.text: The whole of America upset Roman dictator

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: the whole means all
US is America

explanation.surface: The whole of America upsets a Roman dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALLUS round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Sulla made himself dictator of Rome in 82 BC.

clue.text: A strange trust one put in numbers, making a bloomer

indicators.note: put in says the pieces go inside the abbreviation for numbers

parts.note: NUM is short for Numbers, the book of the Bible

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of a trust come out oddly ordered

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A strange trust put into numbers leads to a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' makes ASTURT from A TRUST; add I and 'put in' NUM. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden plant with bright trumpet blooms is a flowering plant, a bloomer.

clue.text: Thought of you and me in the sea

indicators.note: in says the pronoun goes inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: You and I thought about being out in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med is the usual crossword shorthand for the Mediterranean, so 'the sea' gives three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so mused means thought, past tense.

definitions.meaning: a boss is a raised ornamental knob

explanation.surface: The boss of the horses is in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a stud on a surface, and a stud is a horse-breeding farm.

clue.text: Usain Bolt arranging the wash and brush-up

indicators.note: arranging says the letters of the sprinter's name are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt is arranging a wash and brush-up.
explanation.walkthrough: USAIN BOLT has exactly the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the act of washing oneself, a wash and tidy-up.

clue.text: Instruments brought back from heinous murder

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instruments are recovered from the scene of a heinous murder.
explanation.walkthrough: SMURD sits across 'heinous murder'; 'brought back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: These percussion pieces are musical instruments struck with sticks.

parts.note: split as E plus a word for country, the name looks like an eastern territory, so the beast seems to come from the East

explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual abbreviation for east, and 'apparently' marks the whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African antelope has spiralled horns; its name only seems to mean an eastern country.

clue.text: One girl and another absorbing heart of Greek epic

parts.note: Thea is a girl's name

indicators.note: absorbing says the second name takes a letter into itself

parts.note: Enid is another girl's name

indicators.note: heart of picks the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: Two girls absorb the heart of a Greek epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' Greek gives E, which ENID is 'absorbing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's poem about the wanderings of a Trojan hero is a Latin epic.
